html:
The only woman ever to rule China as emperor in her own name. She held power for about half a century, first behind her husband and then on the throne from 690 to 705.

She began as a junior concubine of Emperor Taizong. After his death she became the favourite of his son, Emperor Gaozong, and was made empress in 655. When Gaozong fell ill she ran the government. After he died in 683 she set aside two of her sons, and in 690 she declared her own Zhou dynasty, breaking the line of the Tang.

  • She widened the imperial examinations and brought in men from outside the old noble families.
  • She backed Buddhism and paid for great works such as the large Buddha at the Longmen Grottoes.
  • She used informers and secret police against rivals.

Old and ill, she was forced to step down in 705, and the Tang was restored. Later Confucian historians judged her harshly; modern ones see a capable ruler.
